segments: and the sons of his brothers, thirty-six souls,
and none were saved except him and forty souls who fled.
And they came and entered into a new house which had been built in the territory of the fortress,
in a place called Kheṣnona in Armenian.
And while they were sitting, distressed, and pondering how they might rescue those of them who were taken captive in the battle,
then all of them agreed:
"Since this battle which took place in this region
occurred because of the Christians,
it is therefore right to exact from them a levy,
and to ransom those who were taken captive on their account."
Then they began to register each city and district for a certain amount of gold,
according to the capacity of the place.
Justice, however, did not tolerate
that their aim should be fulfilled in act,
but quickly caused that new house to collapse upon them,
and destroyed them all equally.
And except for one man, a gatekeeper,
upon whose side a beam fell,
and threw him outside the gate of that house,
no other person of them was saved.
And at the beginning of the year one thousand and six hundred and one [1290 AD],
Ala-Almish, the lord of Mayperqaṭ,
who was also a great persecutor of the Christians,
sent secretly and killed the lord of Mush,
a Christian man,
Armenian by race,
and he inflicted other evils upon the monks of Mar Qoma.
One of the monks there took courage in himself
and went to the camp,
and slandered Ala-Almish.
And he gained open access to the King of Kings,
who used to listen to him kindly.
And on one of the days, while the King of Kings was riding and crossed over a certain bridge on the River Kura,
the monk seized the bridle of his horse and swore:
"I will not let you pass until you command that Ala-Almish be killed!"
And in that very hour he gave the command, and he was killed.
And in those same days, furthermore, an Egyptian jurist {nomikos}, a courageous man,
who was known as Faraj Allah,
and who was a secretary in Mosul, drew near,
and exposed {OCR?} the deceit of the Persian jurist, Abd al-Mumin, whom we mentioned above,
and that he had unjustly killed Mas'ud bar Qawṭi,
and inflicted great evils upon the Christians,
and collected a large tribute for himself.
And when the King of Kings commanded that his case be investigated,
the Persian was found guilty and killed,
and the justice of God was terribly avenged upon him.
